mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate is historically low at 0.97%, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active without condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of time periods, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% signals monetary easing, compressing discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal activates when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is below 1.0% and unemployment rate exceeds 6.0%, it indicates recessionary pressure suppressing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal activates when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
